partition_proof.exhaustive: Each deterministic stage either succeeds or fails. If any stage fails, the finite total order has a unique least failing stage, placing the input in exactly one C0-C8 class. If none fails, the input is in C9.
partition_proof.disjoint: Classes C0-C8 are keyed by the unique least failing stage; C9 has no failing stage. Therefore no input belongs to two classes.
partition_proof.fail_closed: By construction the verifier returns before CAS1/CAS2 on C0-C8, so mutation=false for every invalid class.
partition_proof.uint_safety: The logical verifier has no wraparound semantics. Canonical uint acceptance requires a nonnegative integer that the concrete verifier can parse within its declared integer domain and round-trip to the unique canonical decimal representation. Any overflow, truncation, sign change, exponent/alternate spelling, or lossy conversion is an L0 failure before mutation.
partition_proof.migration_seed_boundary: The seed rule is a one-blob exception, not a reusable generation value. The exact legacy seed blob maps to generation 0 once; its committed successor is generation 1, and this newly committed successor is generation 2. Therefore stale seed records cannot become current through logical-state ABA.
